title: Sign-out invalidates the session on Clerk and the middleware refuses subsequent requests
asA: operator who wants sign-out to actually mean the session is gone
iWant: the Clerk-initiated sign-out to invalidate my session such that a subsequent request carrying the same cookie is refused
soThat: a leaked cookie stops working the moment I have signed out

acceptanceCriteria.description: After a Clerk-initiated sign-out (client-side call to Clerk's `signOut` or an equivalent server-invoked revocation), a request to a protected route carrying the pre-sign-out `__session` cookie is refused by the middleware.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an operator who has signed in and holds a valid `__session` cookie, then invokes the project's sign-out surface which calls Clerk's `signOut`
acceptanceCriteria.when: a subsequent request replays the same `__session` cookie against a protected route
acceptanceCriteria.then: the middleware treats the request as unauthenticated; the response status is 401 (API) or a redirect (page); the handler is never invoked

acceptanceCriteria.description: An administrative revoke performed on the Clerk dashboard has the same effect: a request replaying the revoked session's cookie is refused.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a valid `__session` cookie for a signed-in operator whose session has just been revoked via the Clerk dashboard
acceptanceCriteria.when: a request replays that cookie against a protected route
acceptanceCriteria.then: the middleware refuses per AC-9107-1; no cache the middleware or session verifier holds keeps the revoked session alive beyond one revocation-propagation cycle (the verifier's `revocationCheckIntervalMs`, documented in ADR-1005; the value is bounded and stated)
